findings.where: First screen, the row of five outlined pills under the lead (PPP Law, Infrastructure, Development banks, Governments, Risk allocation), desktop and phone
findings.fault: The pills do nothing when clicked, yet they look like filter chips or links. They have a white outline and white label, the same white as the email button just below them, and parts.txt shows they are not actionable. A visitor will click 'PPP Law' expecting his PPP work or articles, and nothing happens. They also add a third row of white shapes between the lead and the one action, so the action is less clearly the only thing on the screen to press.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer on a first visit, who clicks a topic to see Mark's work on it and gets nothing, and who reads five button-like shapes as five more choices next to 'write to me'.

findings.where: Article specimen: the gap from the photo caption to the subhead 'So, what are the key ‘chapter topics’?', the three-item list, and the hairline under it (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The vertical spacing breaks down exactly where the brief asked it to hold. The subhead sits right under the caption with no space above it, so it reads as part of the caption block. The list items are set much tighter than the body text, and their wrapped lines run together. The hairline below the list touches its last line. Adding an image, caption, list and subhead (the specimen's whole test) visibly upsets the spacing.
findings.who_objects: The founder and Angélique. The brief requires spacing that survives her adding an image, caption, list or subhead. This specimen shows it does not, so every article she posts would look cramped and unfinished to Mark's readers.

findings.where: Article specimen: the orange-red list bullets and the orange-red underlined link 'Streamlining the PPP Process: Meeting the ‘Abundance’ Challenge'
findings.fault: A third, warm orange-red appears that belongs nowhere in the house palette. The candidate's own palette says 'Four colours and no accent', with house blue for links. So this link is coloured differently from the page's other link ('Play again', in blue), and the article, which is the product, steps outside the blue-and-grey identity.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who asked for every tile to be built in the house blue and grey with at most one accent. A reader also loses the one link colour that tells them what is clickable.

findings.where: First screen ground: the diagonal stripe pattern over the whole blue field (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The field is not the one flat blue field this direction calls for. Fine diagonal stripes run across all of it, behind the heading, lead text and portrait, which makes the ground busy and a little technical. The tile contradicts itself: its Texture panel and motion sketch both show a flat field and say 'No texture: one flat field, no grain and no gradient.'
findings.who_objects: Mark, who dislikes busy sites and is not an engineer ('nothing in-your-face techy'). Also the founder, who will judge this tile from its own claim and find the first screen doesn't match it.

findings.where: First screen: the giant pale ghost letters 'PPP' behind the heading (behind 'In my view, we are at…' on desktop, and at the right of the heading on phone)
findings.fault: An oversized watermark acronym sits under Mark's line and overlaps its letters. It muddies the strongest element on the screen and reads as a decorative gimmick, a second ornament on top of the stripes, instead of the plain large serif line the brief asks for.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who asked for refined, never novelty, and for scale contrast instead of extra elements. A visitor reads Mark's line through faint letters that compete with it.

findings.fault: Two nav items name near-synonymous places for Mark's writing. A visitor can't tell which holds the papers they want, or why there are two.
findings.who_objects: A procurement reader looking for Mark's publications, who has to guess between two labels or open both.

findings.where: First screen action: the arrow '→' after 'Mark.Moseley@MMMinfra.com' in the white button
findings.fault: The arrow signals 'go to another page', but the action writes an email. The label already shows the address, and the arrow suggests a different outcome from the one the visitor gets.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who expects a contact page and instead gets their mail client opening.

findings.where: Type pair panel (desktop): 'In my view, Gelasio' on the left and 'Source Sans 3' on the right
findings.fault: The two specimens start at different heights: the Source Sans sample sits well below the Gelasio one. The pair reads as misaligned rather than as two matched columns.
findings.who_objects: The founder reviewing the style tile, who reads loose alignment as unfinished work.
